rows.t: Vintage Cast Iron Dove — Painted Cream Bird on Pedestal Base, Distressed Rustic

det.desc: A dove with some miles on it, and proud of them. This heavy cast iron bird stands on a square pedestal base with a carved rope-and-gadroon edge, its wings folded in neat carved rows, its head turned as if it just heard something. The casting is two pieces bolted together at the base, hollow underneath with the center hex bolt visible in the underside photos — solid, stable, and heavy in the hand the way cast iron should be. No maker's mark is visible. Whether it is a genuinely older garden piece or a vintage-style casting made to look the part, we can't prove from the photos, so it is priced and sold honestly as a decorative bird with a great aged finish. Use it as a paperweight that means business, a shelf or mantel accent, a garden ornament, or a quiet little sculpture among plants and pottery. rows.t: Olaf Willums Nyhavn Wood Engraving 1915 Pencil Signed Norwegian Print

det.desc: Olaf Willums (1886-1967), Norwegian painter and printmaker, co-founder of the Association of Norwegian Printmakers. "Nyhavn," a wood engraving from 1915: the bow of a ship and the gabled houses along the Nyhavn canal in Copenhagen. Pencil-signed and dated 1915 at lower right, titled "Fra Nyhavn" at lower left, with the artist's monogram below the signature. The Victoria and Albert Museum holds an impression of this print. This impression was issued with The International Studio, Vol. LXI, May 1917 (John Lane, New York), printed on heavy toned paper. It is a genuine impression from the block, checked under a loupe: hand-cut line work, ink sitting in the blacks, no halftone dots. Sheet measures 8 x 11.75 inches; the image measures 4 x 7.5 inches. The leaf has small stab-binding holes along the left margin from the magazine binding, clear of the image. The back is blank. Ships flat with rigid support.

det.desc: This is vintage sheet music for "Blue Tango," a piano solo composed by Leroy Anderson. This specific edition was published in 1951 by Mills Music, in New York. It was the first instrumental recording to sell over one million copies and reached number one on the Billboard charts, staying there for 38 weeks. It is a light orchestral/concert piece that uses a rhythm reflective of an Argentinian tango. Leroy Anderson (1908–1975) was a highly educated American composer known for his classically-trained background and clever "light" orchestral works.
